thread:
Priya: FYI ACME Prod reported a ~3m window of 429s on their dedicated pool at 13:02 UTC. Customer says traffic spiked to 2.8x usual and their app saw timeouts/429s.

Alyssa: Ticket #ACME-842 opened. They attached sample request ids and response headers: 'x-rw-error: rate_limited', 'x-rw-warmup: true'. They say retries didn't help.

Miguel: Can you paste the autoscaler logs and pool config? suspect warm pool or min_replicas boundary.

Priya: Pasting the pool config snippet the customer provided:
```
pool: acme-prod-dedicated
min_replicas: 3
max_replicas: 40
scale_cooldown_sec: 120
warmup_enabled: true
warmup_target: 2
```

Alyssa: infra-bot dump of events (filtered):
```
[13:02:12] autoscaler: scale-request desired=18 current=3 reason=throughput_spike
[13:02:12] autoscaler: enqueue scale job id=xyz holdoff=120s
[13:03:30] kube: pulling image redwood-runtime:v2026-02 -> backoff 30s (registry 429)
[13:04:00] autoscaler: scale-request blocked: min_replicas enforced; warmup pending true
[13:05:20] infra: node-attach delayed: attach-queue-length=8
[13:05:30] autoscaler: scale applied -> new_replicas=12
```

Miguel: Two things jump out: (1) scale_cooldown 120s + holdoff caused delayed start of many workers, (2) image pull/backoff from registry + attach queue slowed provisioning. That combination makes it look like autoscaler "too slow" even though it accepted desired > current.

Sam: Looking at cluster metrics, we had a transient GC on the attach service and ECR (third-party registry) throttled pulls for a minute. node attach latency spiked to 22s. noisy neighbor? Possibly another pool doing bulk node provisioning at same time.

Priya: Customer timeline: 13:02 first 429s, 13:06 errors stop, full recovery by 13:08. They reported 4m impact window.

Frank: I temporarily applied a burst override to the pool at 13:05 to expedite scale (bumped min_replicas to 8, bypassed warmup). Confirmed queue draining and 429s dropped.

Alyssa: Customer notified and appreciative. They want root cause analysis and mitigations so this doesn't recur.

Miguel: Repro steps we have so far:
1) Configure pool with small min_replicas (3) and long scale_cooldown (>=120s).
2) Simulate 3x qps burst.
3) Simultaneously throttle image registry (force short image-pull backoffs).
4) Observe autoscaler queueing and delayed replica readiness -> transient 429s.

Sam: Additional platform note: if other pools start heavy node provisioning at same time, attach service queueing becomes a bottleneck. That's consistent with noisy neighbor. I can reproduce locally by firing two heavy scaleouts concurrently.

Miguel: Short-term mitigations we recommended to customer and applied where possible:
- Increase min_replicas for bursty routes
- Lower scale_cooldown to 20s for that pool
- Enable pre-warm pool (increase warmup_target) for predictable spikes
- If using third-party registries, mirror images to our internal cache to avoid pulls during surge

Alyssa: Also flagged a UI setting request: allow customers to enable an "emergency burst" toggle that temporarily bypasses cool-down/holdoff.

Frank: Action items for eng teams:
- Miguel: add better autoscaler logs to show "blocked reason" (holdoff/min_replicas/image-pull) in metric labels (ETA 1 week).
- Sam: investigate attach service scaling + ECR mirror fallback (ETA 2 weeks).
- Infra: add a runbook for oncall to apply temporary burst overrides safely (short-term doc updated).

Miguel: For the reproducible test I'll create a small harness that simulates registry backoffs + synthetic bursts so QA can validate fixes.

Sam: I found a related metric gap: we don't emit per-pool image-pull backoff counts to the console; adding that will help detection.

Priya: Customer asked for a postmortem and timeline. We'll draft and include mitigation suggestions.

Alyssa: Notes to include in the customer PM: cause = provisioning pipeline bottleneck (image-pull + attach queue) + conservative autoscaler cooldown + low min_replicas for bursty workload => delayed scale. Remediation applied (temporary min bump) and permanent fixes planned.

infra-bot: autoticket created: INFRA-647 mirror-cache-ecr, assigned to Sam.

billing-bot: customer usage spike logged; no billing anomalies.

Priya: Closing loop: customer confirmed normalized and will test new warmup settings in staging. We'll follow up after Miguel's harness.

Frank: I'll leave a short note on oncall channel with the runbook link and the exact override command used: `redwoodctl pool override-burst acme-prod --min 8 --ttl 10m`

Alyssa: Thanks team. I'll mark ticket ACME-842 as "mitigated - monitoring" and attach this thread.

Miguel: Filing a follow-up RFC to propose autoscaler improvements (better holdoff heuristics + image-pull awareness).

Sam: I'll start the ECR mirror experiment in a dev cluster and report results.

Priya: End of thread.
